chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated that Abu Muhammad Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated that Al-Abbas ibn al-Faraj narrated that Abu Salmah al-Ghifari narrated to me that Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Furat narrated from Abdul Malik ibn Marwan

He said: We were with Muawiyah one day, and a group of Quraysh had gathered with him, including several from Banu Hashim. Muawiyah said: O Banu Hashim, with what do you boast over us? Is not the father and mother one? And the home and birthplace one?

Ibn Abbas said: We boast over you for the same reason that you boast over the rest of Quraysh, and Quraysh boast over the Ansar, and the Ansar boast over the rest of the Arabs, and the Arabs boast over the rest of the Ajam (non-Arabs): because of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and for what you cannot deny nor escape from.

Muawiyah said: O Ibn Abbas, you have been given a fluent tongue, you almost overpower the truth of others with your falsehood. Ibn Abbas said: Hush, for falsehood does not overpower the truth, and leave off jealousy, for indeed jealousy is a bad slogan.

Muawiyah said: You speak the truth. By God, I love you for four characteristics, in addition to forgiving you for four deeds. As for the first, I love you because of your kinship with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). As for the second, you are a man from my family and my household and from the sucklings of Abd Manaf. As for the third, my father was a friend to your father. As for the fourth, you are the tongue of Quraysh, their leader, and their jurist.

As for the four I forgive you for: your enmity towards me at Siffin among those who attacked, your fault in abandoning Uthman among those who did wrong, your effort against Ayesha, mother of the believers, among those who strove, and your rejection of Ziyad from me among those who rejected.

I struck the nose and eye of this matter until I extracted your excuse from the Book of God, the Exalted, and the words of the poets. As for what matched the Book of God, it is His saying: 'They mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil.' And as for what the poets said, it is the words of my brother from Banu Dhubyan: 'And I do not anticipate a brother whom you do not blame for the fuzz (minor faults) of any refined man.'

So know that I have accepted the first four for you, and forgiven you the last four, and I was in that as the first poet said: 'I accept the good from those I love, and forgive what else they have done.'

Then Ibn Abbas spoke, after praising God and glorifying Him, and said: As for what you mentioned that you love me because of my kinship with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), that is incumbent upon you and every Muslim who believes in God and His Messenger, because it is the reward which the Messenger of God asked you for regarding what He gave you of illumination and clear proofs. So He, the Exalted, said: 'Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it except love for the near of kin.'
Whoever does not respond to the Messenger of God to what he asked for, he will be doomed, disgraced, and fall headlong into Hell.

As for what you mentioned that I am a man from your family and your household, that is so, and you intended by it the maintaining of kinship ties. By my life, indeed you are today maintaining kinship from what was from you, for which there is no blame upon you today.

As for your saying that my father was a friend to your father, that was indeed the case, and the first poet's words preceded it: 'I will maintain loyalty to him whom my father befriended in his life, and maintain it for him after him among the relatives. I am not for one who does not keep the covenant, nor will I say a word that is not with him at the times of calamity.'

As for what you mentioned that I am the tongue of Quraysh, their leader, and their jurist, I was not given anything of that except that I was given it, except that you refused by your nobility and generosity except to prefer me. And the first poet's words preceded it: 'And every noble person prefers the nobles, considering them worthy even if they are superior.'

As for what you mentioned of my enmity towards you at Siffin, by God, if I had not done that, I would have been among the worst of creatures. Could your soul tell you, O Muawiyah, that I would abandon my cousin, the Commander of the Faithful and Master of the Muslims, while the Emigrants and Helpers and the chosen best had gathered for him? No, O Muawiyah! Would I doubt my religion? Or be confused in my nature? Or be stingy with myself?

As for what you mentioned of abandoning Uthman, he was abandoned by those who were closer in kinship to him than I, and were a model for the near and distant relatives. And I did not return upon him with those who attacked, but I held back from him, as the people of Marwah and Hijra held back.

As for what you mentioned of my effort against Ayesha, indeed God the Exalted commanded her to remain in her house and veil herself with her veil. When she uncovered the veil of modesty and disobeyed her Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), we did what was from us towards her.

As for what you mentioned of the rejection of Ziyad, I did not reject him, but the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) rejected him when he said: 'The child belongs to the bed, and for the fornicator is the stone.' And after this, I love what pleases you in all your affairs.

Amr ibn al-As spoke and said: O Commander of the Faithful, by God, I do not love you for a moment, except that he has been given a fluent tongue, so he turns his heart as he wishes. And my example and his example are as the first poet said, and he cited a verse of poetry.

Ibn Abbas said: Indeed Amr is between the bones and meat, the stick and the bark, and he has spoken, so let him listen, for he has matched his peer. By God, O Amr, I hate you for God and I do not excuse myself from it. You stood as a speaker and said: 'I am the hater of Muhammad.' So God the Exalted revealed: 'Indeed your enemy is the one cut off.' So you are cut off from religion and the world, and you are the hater of Muhammad in the Age of Ignorance and in Islam.

And God the Blessed and Exalted said: 'You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger.' And you opposed God and His Messenger, anciently and recently. And you exerted yourself against the Messenger of God with your exertion, and you roused against him with your cavalry and infantry, until when God overpowered you in your affair and returned your plot to your neck, and weakened your strength and falsified your news, you departed while you are weak.

Then you nearly with your exertion for the enmity of the family of his Prophet after him. It is not in you, in that, love for Muawiyah or the family of Muawiyah, except enmity for God the Exalted and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), along with your old hatred and jealousy for the sons of Abd Manaf.

And your example in that is as the first poet said: 'Amr exposed himself to me, and Amr exposed himself as a disgrace. The she-camel of the desert exposed herself to the visiting lion. He is not my equal so I will not insult his honor, nor is he my servant so I will strike the servant.'
Amr ibn al-As spoke, but Muawiyah cut him off and said: By God, O Amr, you are not one of his match. If you wish, speak, and if you wish, stop.

Amr took the opportunity and was silent. Ibn Abbas said: Let him be, O Muawiyah, by God, I will fatten him with a branding iron, his disgrace and his mark will remain upon him until the Day of Resurrection, the maids and slaves will speak of it, and it will be recited in gatherings and discussed in assemblies.

Then Ibn Abbas said: O Amr, and began to speak. Muawiyah extended his hand and placed it on the mouth of Ibn Abbas, and said to him: I swear to you, O Ibn Abbas, that you hold back. He disliked that the people of Syria should hear what Ibn Abbas was saying.
And while he was in that state, Ibn Abbas said: Be gone, O servant, and you are blameworthy. Then they separated.

key_terms.الْمَوَدَّةُ فِي الْقُرْبَى: Love for the near of kin, a key verse cited for Ahl al-Bayt's right
key_terms.خِذْلَانُ عُثْمَانَ: Abandonment of Uthman, referring to not actively helping him against rebels
key_terms.سَعْيٌ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ: Effort/striving against Ayesha, referring to the Battle of the Camel
key_terms.صِفِّين: Siffin, the site of the Battle of Camel/Siffin where Ali fought Muawiyah
key_terms.لِسَانُ قُرَيْشٍ: Tongue of Quraysh, a title for the eloquent speaker/leader
key_terms.نَفْيُ زِيَادٍ: Rejection of Ziyad, referring to denying his lineage as Muawiyah's brother

ai.seo_question: What were the four characteristics Muawiyah liked in Ibn Abbas and the four deeds he forgave him for?
ai.summary: This dialogue from *Al-Khisal* highlights the theological and political tension between the Umayyad claim to power and the Hashemite claim to spiritual authority, with Ibn Abbas grounding his status in the Quranic verse of *Mawadda al-Qurba* (42:23). The narrative serves as a Shia apologetic, reinterpreting Ibn Abbas’s historical actions at Siffin and regarding Uthman as consistent with divine will rather than political opportunism. It concludes with a sharp critique of Amr ibn al-As, linking his political maneuvering to the Quranic concept of *Shan'i* (the enemy) in Surah Al-Kawthar.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-35 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan quoted Abu Muhammad Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Al-Ab’bas ibn al-Faraj, on the authority of Abu Salmat al-Qaffari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ibrahimibn Abi Forut, on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Marvan,

“Once I was with Muawiyah and a group of the people from the Quraysh tribe were there. Some of the Hashemites were among them. Muawiyah said, “O Hashemites! Why do you think you are better than us while we both come from the same father and mother, and we both come from the same family and country?”

Ibn Abbas said, “We say we are better than you for the same reason that you say you are better than the Quraysh, and the Quraysh say they are better than the Helpers (Ansar), and the Helpers (Ansar) say they are better than the Arabs, and the Arabs say they are better than the non-Arabs. That is we are proud because of God’s Prophet (MGB). You can neither deny this nor escape from this fact.”

Muawiyah said, “O Ibn Abbas! You have been granted such a convincing tongue with which you press your false accusations over the truth.”Ibn Abbas said, “Shut up! Indeed falsehood can never overcome the truth. Quit being jealous as jealousy is bad.”

Muawiyah said, “You spoke the truth. I swear by God that I like you for four characteristics and I forgive you for four deeds. The four reasons I like you for are: First of all I like you because of your close relationship to God’s Prophet (MGB). The second reason is that you are a man from my family and from the pure race of Abd Manaf. The third reason is that my father was friends with your father. The fourth reason is that you are the speaker for the Quraysh tribe and you are their learned man. And your four deeds which I forgive you for are: your taking part in the Battle of Siffin along with those who attacked me; your ugly act being not assisting Uthman against the rebels who attacked him, and your attempts against Ayesha , plus your rejection of Zyad being my step-brother.

When I considered your wicked deeds in detail, I found an excuse for your deeds from the Book of the Honorable the Exalted God and one from Arab poems. Your excuse based on the Book (Quran) comes from the following verse, ‘Others (there are who) have acknowledged their wrong-doings: they have mixed an act that was good with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn unto them (in Mercy): for Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.’ Your excuse based on Arab poems comes from the words of the Zebyan tribe who said, ‘Which of your brothers can you find free of faults. You will be left without any friends if you cut off relations for small faults.’ You should know that I have recognized your four good characteristics and have forgiven your four deeds as the poet said, ‘I accept good deeds from my loved ones. I forgive them for whatever else they may have done.’”

When he finished, Ibn Abbas started to respond by first reciting God’s praises and glorifications. Then he said, ‘You mentioned that you like me because I am close to God’s Prophet (MGB). This is incumbent upon you and all Muslims who believe in God and His Prophet (MGB), since this love is the reward which God’s Prophet (MGB) asked for in return for what he brought you in terms of illumination and clear reasoning. The Honorable the Exalted God says, ‘…Say: "No reward do I ask of you for this except the love of those near of kin.’ Whoever doesn’t follow this verse and doesn’t love his near of kin is going to be hopeless, without honor and in Hell.

You mentioned that you like me because I am a man from your family. Well, that is right. You wanted to perform your duty and visit your relations of kin. You seem to be doing a lot of that these days. You are not to be blamed today for your past mistakes.

You mentioned that you like me because my father was friends with your father. That is right and it is certified by what the poet said about it:I will strive to be loyal to my friend for as long as he is aliveAnd shall do so with his relatives should he die and I stay aliveWhoever honors not his pledge, I shall not trustSince then he shall not pacify my swollen heart.

You mentioned that you like me because I am the speaker for the Quraysh tribe and I am their learned man. You likewise have a similar rank. However, you are so noble as to mention me to be of such a rank. This is also supported by what the poet said about it:Noble ones set other ones up higher than themselvesThey honor others though they are nobler themselves

You mentioned my animosity with you, since I attacked you at Siffin. By God, I would have been amongst the worst creatures in the world had I not done so. O Muawiyah! How could you even imagine that I would abandon my cousin Ali - the Commander of the Faithful and the Master of the Muslims - who was supported by the Emigrants (Muhajerin), the Helpers (Ansar), and the cream of the crop of the freedom-lovers, and join you! O Muawiyah! Then I would have serious doubts about my faith in my religion, my moral constitution and myself.

You mentioned that I abandoned Uthman. Well, even those who were much closer to him abandoned him and left. I followed his close associates and those who were not so close to him. I never assisted the rebels who revolted against him. I just abandoned him.

You mentioned my effort made against Ayesha . You know that she had been ordered by the Sublime God’s Prophet (MGB) to stay behind the veil at home, but she tore the veil, left her house and opposed the Prophet (MGB). The way we treated with her was appropriate.

You mentioned my rejection of your step-brotherhood with Zyad. However, this was not my denial but the Prophet’s denial since he (MGB) has said, ‘the offspring belongs to the owner of the bed and the fornicatress gets stoned.’ Now I like to do what would please you, whatever it may be.’

Then Amr Ibn Al-A’as started to talk and said, ‘O commander of the faithful (referring to Muawiyah!) By God, he doesn’t like you and just wants to fool you into thinking that he agrees with you using his sharp tongue. He cited the poems to support this.’
Then Ibn Abbas said, ‘Indeed Amr put himself to great trouble. He should now know that he is facing a strong opponent.’

Then Ibn Abbas added, ‘O Amr! I swear by God that I am opposed to you for the sake of God and I shall not apologize for that. You had said, ‘I hate Muhammad.’ The Honorable the Exalted God revealed, ‘For he who hateth thee, he will be cut off (from Future Hope).’You have been cut off from the religion and the world. You even hated Muhammad in the Age of Ignorance!Indeed the Blessed the Sublime God says, ‘Thou wilt not find any people who believe in Allah and the Last Day, loving those who resist Allah and His Messenger…’ Indeed you have always resisted God and God’s Prophet (MGB). You did whatever you could against the Prophet of God (MGB). You gathered all your forces - on foot or riding - against the Prophet (MGB) until God defeated you, hanged up your sign of deception around your neck, reduced your strength and rejected your way. That is why you turned around and changed your approach and re-directed your plans of animosity with the members of the Holy Household of the Prophet (MGB). Therefore, you united with Muawiyah for this goal. However, you should know that love for the household of Muawiyah and no others is nothing but animosity with the Honorable the Exalted God and His Prophet (MGB). You still have your old animosity with and jealousy of the progeny of Abd Manaf as the poet says,Amr blamed me but he himself was debasedNear a male lion he turned into a weak hyenaHe doesn’t equal me so I shall not fight himHe is not my servant so I can’t punish him!
Amr Ibn Al-A’as wanted to reply but Muawiyah stopped him and said, ‘O Amr! I swear by God that you cannot match him. It would be best for you to stop it.’

Amr Ibn Al-A’as used this opportunity and became silent. Ibn Abbas said, ‘O Muawiyah! Please I beseech by God! Please let him start talking. Then I shall debase him so much that the masters and the slaves cite his case and restate his story in meetings and parties up until the Resurrection Day.’

Then Ibn Abbas started to speak and said, ‘O Amr!’ However, Muawiyah put his hand on Ibn Abbas’s mouth and said, ‘O Ibn Abbas! I swear to you to finish this since I do not like the Syrians to hear this speech.’
Then Ibn Abbas told Amr, ‘O blameworthy servant! Get lost.’
Then they left.”
